design_role.name: pilot
design_role.purpose: Estimate the design quantities required to preregister a genuinely powered confirmatory replication while preserving the original randomized three-arm, two-origin protocol.
design_role.reason: The original primary estimand is per important seeded defect, but the important-defect denominator per task was not fixed and the baseline escape probability and reviewer/matched-task dependence were not empirically known. Therefore confirmatory decidability was unknown before data collection.

planning_inputs_to_estimate: important seeded defects per task and total important-defect denominator per arm
escape probability by condition, task family, and artifact-origin side
power.replication_sample_size_rule: After the pilot is frozen and reported, compute candidate confirmatory sample sizes from the frozen planning estimates under explicitly stated assumptions, choose the estimand and inferential method, and preregister a separate replication before observing any replication outcomes.

effective_preregistration.prediction: The original directional hypothesis is retained as an exploratory prediction: the Doubt gate may show lower important-defect escape than ordinary review and the active placebo. Experiment 001 cannot promote or kill the effectiveness claim from that direction alone.
effective_preregistration.primary_metric: Pilot planning estimand: observed per-defect escape probability for preregistered medium/high defects, together with the realized important-defect denominator, task-level any-escape probability, false alarms, review time, and dependence diagnostics. Three-arm contrasts are exploratory planning estimates, not confirmatory effectiveness tests.
effective_preregistration.uncertainty_method: Publish raw task rows and descriptive uncertainty for condition contrasts while preserving reviewer and matched-task identifiers. With the pilot minimum of 12 reviewer IDs, interval coverage is not treated as confirmatory; clustering/dependence estimates are planning inputs for the separately preregistered powered replication.
effective_preregistration.kill_condition: Experiment 001 may retire or narrow the experimental design if randomization, control parity, endpoint coverage, seed realism, record integrity, or denominator/dependence estimation fails. It does not make a confirmatory promote-or-kill decision on the H-level effectiveness claim; exploratory adverse or null effects must still be reported in full.
effective_preregistration.stop_condition: Stop the pilot at exactly 432 scorable reviews per reviewer cohort, with the existing preregistered replacement policy and no outcome-driven extension. Freeze and report the realized important-defect denominator, arm/family/origin rates, dependence diagnostics, false alarms, and review-time costs before designing any powered replication.
effective_preregistration.promotion_rule: Experiment 001 may promote only measured pilot-design statements: realized denominators, observed arm/family/origin rates, dependence diagnostics, false-alarm and review-time distributions, and feasibility findings. It may not promote the Doubt gate as effective, safer, better, or as having passed the original 10-point effect region. Any effectiveness promotion requires a separate powered preregistration and later independent replication.

effect_region.note: The original 10-point escape-reduction / 10-point false-alarm thresholds are preserved in preregistration.json as correction history and a planning reference. They are not a pilot promotion gate.

required_outputs: realized important-defect denominator per condition, family, and artifact-origin side
